name: Neo4j Backup Job
description: Creating or updating a Neo4jBackup CR runs exactly one Job per one-time backup (or a CronJob spawning one Job per scheduled firing), records the outcome in status.history, and never stands up a long-running backup pod.

steps.note: User creates/updates a Neo4jBackup CR naming instanceRef, database/allDatabases/shardedDatabase scope, storage, and optional schedule
Validates the spec, resolves the target cluster/standalone, checks readiness/suspend, runs sharded preflight
One-time backups: creates the single Job running neo4j-admin backup
Scheduled backups: creates/updates the CronJob that spawns a Job per firing
Emitted when the one-time backup Job is created
Emitted when the CronJob is created/updated
On Job completion, parses the backup pod log and appends a BackupRun to status.history
Emitted when the backup Job succeeds
Emitted when the backup Job fails terminally

name: Neo4j Restore Job
description: Creating a Neo4jRestore CR resolves a backup source and drives either a standalone offline neo4j-admin Job, a cluster in-place Cypher recreate, or a per-database all-databases restore loop, then brings the restored database(s) back online.

steps.note: Staff creates a Neo4jRestore CR naming instanceRef, source (backupRef or storage), and options
Resolves the target, checks terminal phases and version compatibility
Validates the request and pins the resolved backup source onto status before branching by target type
Resolves spec.source.backupRef to a StorageLocation + BackupsPath via the referenced Neo4jBackup's status.history
Cluster targets: issues dbms.recreateDatabase and polls until online
All-databases cluster restores: recreates one database per reconcile pass from the backup's per-database artifact map
Standalone targets: scales the instance to 0 and runs an offline neo4j-admin restore Job
Emitted when the restore Job or Cypher recreate is issued
On success, restarts the instance, registers/starts the restored database(s), runs post-restore hooks
Emitted when the restore reaches Completed
Emitted when the restore fails terminally

name: Sharded Database Seeding
description: A Neo4jShardedDatabase CR's spec.seedBackupRef is resolved into per-shard seed URIs — a cloud directory URI, or an operator-managed PVC HTTP proxy — so the sharded CREATE DATABASE can seed every graph and property shard from a prior backup.

steps.note: User sets spec.seedBackupRef on a Neo4jShardedDatabase CR (or spec.replaceExisting+force for a destructive re-seed of an existing one)
Validates config and checks the cluster's property-sharding readiness
Looks up the referenced Neo4jBackup's Succeeded run and its per-shard/per-family artifacts
Cloud backups become per-shard cloud seedURIs; PVC backups spin up a busybox-httpd proxy Deployment+Service serving each shard's .backup file
Emitted while waiting for the referenced Neo4jBackup to produce a Succeeded run
Emitted while waiting for the PVC seed-proxy Deployment to become Ready
Issues CYPHER 25 CREATE DATABASE ... SET GRAPH SHARD ... SET PROPERTY SHARDS ... OPTIONS { seedURI: ... }
Emitted once the sharded database is operational; the PVC seed proxy (if any) is then torn down

name: Replica Promotion
description: A Neo4jReplicaPromotion CR performs a one-shot, irreversible promotion of a Neo4jReplicaDatabase's cross-cluster replica into a standalone read-write database, using a check-promote-check-record sequence for crash safety — typically during a DR failover.

steps.note: Staff creates a Neo4jReplicaPromotion CR naming replicaRef (a Neo4jReplicaDatabase)
Observes the live database type, calls PromoteReplicaDatabase, and re-observes before recording completion
Emitted before the irreversible promotion call, warning that in-flight replication lag becomes permanent
Emitted once the live database type is confirmed no longer replica
The Neo4jReplicaDatabase controller's own reconcile independently detects the type change and marks the replica CR terminal Promoted

name: Reconcile Neo4jUser password and role state

steps.note: Neo4jUser reconciler picks up a create/update to the CR (or a requeue) and drives it toward its desired state.
Inline validator checks username shape, requires an auth provider, and treats a not-yet-applied password Secret as Pending rather than Failed.
If the user does not yet exist in Neo4j, CREATE USER is issued with staged password/status/home-database/auth-provider clauses.
If the user already exists, only the attributes that drifted from spec (password hash, suspended status, home database, external auth) are ALTERed.
Desired roles not yet granted are added via GRANT ROLE; roles no longer desired are removed via REVOKE ROLE (never touching the implicit PUBLIC role).
Once granted roles match spec.roles exactly and no roles are missing, the reconciler emits UserReady and sets status.phase=Ready.

notes: Neo4jUser.spec is authoritative for password (via the Secret's change-detection hash), accountStatus, homeDatabase, and roles — drift from any of these is reverted every reconcile loop. Privileges are never set here: they live exclusively on Neo4jRole.spec.privileges, never on Neo4jUser or Neo4jRoleBinding.

name: Aura instance provisioning
description: Validate the organization's Aura API credentials, then create or adopt the Aura cloud instance and track it through to Running via the instance phase status flow.

steps.note: AuraProviderConfigReconciler proves the referenced credentials work (token exchange + ListInstances) before any instance create is attempted
AuraInstanceReconciler.observeOrCreate lists instances by name first, then creates via v1 CreateInstance or v2beta1 CreateInstanceV2 when multiDatabase is requested
Progress is tracked via the sfw-aura-instance-phase status flow on this entity

name: Aura multi-database lifecycle
description: Create a database on a multi-database Aura instance, confirm it reconciles to Ready, and track it via the database phase status flow; optionally back it up and restore it in place through the paired per-database CRDs.

steps.note: the referenced AuraInstance must be Ready and probed/created with multiDatabase:true before a database can target it (aura_multidatabase.go)
creates or adopts the database via the v2beta1 API, refusing when the instance's multiDatabase verdict is explicitly false
Progress is tracked via the sfw-aura-database-phase status flow on this entity
optional: takes an on-demand per-database backup once the database is Ready
optional: restores the database in place from a backup, one-shot and non-retryable once submitted

name: Network-Mode CCDR Setup
description: An operator enables the CCDR proxy on the upstream cluster, exchanges CA trust both directions, and creates a network-mode Neo4jReplicaDatabase on the downstream cluster that streams continuously from the upstream's published proxy addresses, instead of pulling a differential backup chain.

steps.note: Operator sets spec.crossClusterReplication.enabled: true and spec.tls.additionalClusterTrustCAs on the upstream cluster
Upstream cluster provisions the HAProxy proxy and publishes status.crossClusterReplication.addresses once its LoadBalancer Service is assigned
Operator creates a Neo4jReplicaDatabase on the downstream cluster with source.mode: network and source.addresses copied from the upstream's status
Downstream reconciler issues CREATE REPLICA DATABASE ... OPTIONS {replicaConfig: {remote, addresses}}
Replica database created and begins streaming from the upstream
